text:
incidents-bot: ALERT - anomalous traffic spike detected on /v1/generate from multiple IP blocks. 5xx and latency spike across edge points. traffic rate 8x normal for a single org key. paging alice oncall.

alice: saw it, looking. rolling up logs now. org-id = org_8X9, started ~2026-03-15T03:10Z according to request traces. lots of short-lived sessions, high tokens per minute.

ben: any obvious UA or pattern? scraper-like?

alice: yeah UA is various but same request fingerprint header X-Client-Fp: ab12.. and payloads show repeated short prompts, high concurrency. looks like automated scraping, maybe credential-stuffing-ish but on API keys rather than logins.

carla: customer rate limits still per-minute + burst. For dedicated customers we also have pool quotas. This one is hitting hosted api endpoints 10k rps for that key. Suggest we apply immediate targeted rate-shape on that API key and add a temporary WAF rule to block obvious IP ranges.

tim: I can push a quick rate-shape policy. Recommend: limit org_8X9 to 20 concurrent requests, 60 r/min for next 30m, and add 429-only policy for overage. Will that break a real customer? check SLAs.

alice: they are a mid-tier sign-up, not enterprise. I think safe to throttle. Also we should disable streaming for that key to reduce head-of-line effects.

ben: preparing WAF ipset. seeing ~120 IPs across two ASN clusters. pushing a geo- and ASN-based block first then tighten to ipset if needed.

incidents-bot: [rule-deploy] waf-rule-2026-03-15-001 created in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. (rule id: r-20260315-001)

carla: applied temporary rate-shape policy: config snippet:
```
policy_id: ps-83X
target: org_8X9
limits:
  concurrency: 20
  rate_per_minute: 60
  burst: 40
mode: rate-shape
duration: 30m
```

alice: applied. noticed 429s starting ~10s after apply. latency 95p improved from 1.2s -> 0.45s at edge, token cost dropping. bots still retrying aggressively though.

tim: pushed disable on streaming for that key: `POST /admin/keys/org_8X9/controls {"streaming": false}` -> 200. that should reduce KV usage.

ben: WAF is blocking top ASN clusters. logs show many retries via different IPs but a big drop already ~60% traffic down.

alice: quick customer impact check: their production apps use sync generation and embeddings. embeddings are also getting hit but lower volume. I've DM'd support to warn of increased 429 for that API key and to prepare to escalate if customer complains.

status-bot: STATUS PAGE UPDATED: "Partial throttling applied to customer org_8X9 due to abusive traffic. Customers on this key may see increased 429s. Investigating."

carla: good. I'll start a temporary quota reset rule to avoid accidental permanent blocks: auto-revert 30m and an alarm if rule still active at 25m.

alice: collecting indicators of compromise for ABUSE team: sample IPs, ASNs, request fingerprint, example payloads. pasting snippets here for handoff:
```
IPs: 198.51.100.12, 203.0.113.45, 45.77.12.9
ASNs: AS13335, AS16509
UA samples: python-requests/2.28, curl/7.85
X-Client-Fp: ab12cd34ef
```

tim: note for runtime: batching queues spiked causing head-of-line latency. rate-shape removed pressure. will monitor memory on kv cache.

ben: added extra blocking rules: block ipset r-ips-scraper-20260315 (120 ips) and tightened WAF bot-score threshold. Rule actions = block + 403 for repeated retries.

incidents-bot: [waf-update] r-20260315-002 applied. Blocked 75 ips so far. Traffic back to ~1.6x baseline.

alice: handoff incoming in 20m to night oncall maria. I'll summarize actions and outstanding tasks:
- Applied rate-shape ps-83X (auto-revert 30m)
- Disabled streaming for org_8X9
- WAF rules r-20260315-001 and r-20260315-002 applied across regions
- Support notified; status page updated
- Collecting sample payloads and ipsets for abuse team

maria: I'll take the night. ETA to be fully up to speed in 10m. questions: any customer escalation already? support? 

alice: support pinged, they queued a PS ticket but no contact yet. if customer reaches out, route to oncall-sre + support lead. escalation matrix in #customer-success.

carla: outstanding: set alert for residual token burn for that org and check billing protection to ensure accidental huge charge not passed to customer. I'll set a spend cap for the key to avoid cost surprises.

tim: creating a short-lived funnel to route all org_8X9 traffic through a hardened path (no caches, strict rate) to gather verified replay evidence. will share access.

maria: thanks. I'll monitor for the next hour and coordinate with abuse team tomorrow morning. please drop final IOCs and the sample payload set in the incidents ticket for handoff.

alice: copying payloads to ticket now. final note: if we see fallback to new IP ranges or credential rotation, we escalate to block ASNs and enforce per-region bans.

ben: also recommend adding a detection rule to match X-Client-Fp ab12cd34ef and throttle earlier in detection pipeline.

maria: acknowledged. taking the channel. marking oncall-handoff done. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident thread archived to #incidents-log. Duration so far: ~60m. export saved at /incidents/exports/1854321000.json"
